answer: For a poll on a kernel mosaic for the forge trellis, the server accepts complete rankings of three options and rejects malformed ballots. It declares a winner only if one option beats each rival head-to-head; otherwise there is no winner. Against 100 identical honest rankings, an attacker needs 101 contrary rankings to make their last choice win, costing submission effort. Automation makes this cheap, and cycles can leave no winner.
